title: Personalized Adolescent Therapy using network-informed approaches (PATH): A Proof-of-Concept Study of a Network-Informed Personalized Treatment Approach
summary:
Many adolescents experience mental health difficulties such as persistent low mood, worries, sleep problems, or problems in everyday life. These difficulties often occur together and can influence each other. Standard psychological treatments are usually based on typical diagnostic categories. In practice, however, adolescents often show very individual combinations of difficulties. Therefore, there is a growing need for treatments that can be better tailored to the individual situation of each young person.

This study investigates a new approach to personalized psychotherapy. At the beginning of treatment, a personal map of the adolescent’s difficulties will be created together with the young person. This map shows which problems are most relevant for the individual and how the different difficulties may be connected. The aim is to better understand which problems may play a particularly important role and where treatment might be most helpful. This personal model will then be systematically used to guide the planning of psychotherapy.

Five adolescents who begin outpatient psychotherapy at the Psychotherapy Outpatient Clinic of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz will take part in the study. Each adolescent will be treated by a licensed child and adolescent psychotherapist. At the beginning of treatment, adolescents will talk about their difficulties and complete short digital questionnaires about their experiences in everyday life. Based on this information, an individual map of their difficulties will be created. This map will be used together with the therapist to tailor the treatment to the adolescent’s individual needs. During therapy, the map will be updated several times to reflect possible changes. Therapists will receive supervision to support the use of this approach. In addition, questionnaires will be used to assess changes in symptoms and treatment experiences.

The aim of the study is to examine whether this personalized approach can be implemented in routine psychotherapy with adolescents, whether it is accepted by adolescents and therapists, and whether it shows first indications of improvements in symptoms. The findings will help to further develop more individualized approaches to psychological treatment for adolescents.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion is transdiagnostic, meaning that participants are eligible regardless of the specific (suspected) disorder, provided that an indication for outpatient psychotherapy has been established during the initial assessment session. Additional inclusion criteria are sufficient German language proficiency and written informed consent from both the participants and their legal guardians.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded if they present with acute suicidality or other crisis conditions requiring immediate treatment, manifest psychotic disorders, severe intellectual disability, or significant cognitive or language impairments that would prevent participation in the assessments.
